correctness.rationale: Four-colour translation orbit reduction, colour S3-symmetry of nonzero colours, and a parity count of root-fixed character phases prove W≡P_G(4) mod16 for all balanced frequencies and zero for unbalanced ones. The known chromatic polynomial algebra and Stirling recurrence prove the exact biclique residue and rank for every m,n≥2. A standalone checker corroborated all 16,932 character values of the 75 labelled graphs through four vertices, all 28,224 balanced biclique coefficients for 2≤m,n≤4, and 99 independent direct sums. The direct C5 witness shows the sufficient criterion is not asserted as necessary.

value.rationale: The Fourier support of a proper-colouring indicator determines exact convolution rank and recoverability on a finite group. The result converts an established graph-orientation parity invariant into a global all-frequency noncancellation criterion and proves a uniform mod-16 rigidity for every biclique with arbitrarily large part sizes, stronger than the trivial translation-forced zeros. Its mathematical object, invariant and motivation are intrinsic, not arbitrary finite slices or table recomputation.
